title: Normalized discrete coefficient module-sheaf model
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, A a commutative ring in universe u, k a Noetherian commutative ring in universe u+1, and e : ULift A ≃+* k. The internal modules on X over the pulled-back discrete condensed ring A [def-sfb-integral-models-stacks-data] have the following normalized presentation on the equivalent coefficient-sized small pro-etale site. There exists a ring sheaf isomorphism c from the constant sheaf k to the reconstructed section ring, whose map on every constant section e(a) is the constant additive sheaf comparison [def-sfb-constant-sheaf-scheme-pullback-comparison] applied to a. The explicitly constructed functor smallModules followed by scalar restriction along c is an additive strong monoidal equivalence. For every module N, the internal finite-constant-model constructibility of N is equivalent to affine-local coefficient-model constructibility of its image [def-sfb-affine-locally-constructible-proetale-modules]. Normalization makes c unique, including on disconnected sites. No derived object, integral completion, residue or Tor predicate occurs.

proof.text: Construct c explicitly: relabel the constant ring k by e inverse, use the inverse constant-sheaf precomposition comparison for AsSmall.down, then precompose the proved discreteRingIso construction of IntegralModelsFlatResidue. Sheafification naturality, constantsIso_unit and discreteRingIso_unit prove the required formula on constants. Keep the existing normalization-uniqueness proof. No arbitrary object is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

Reuse the existing additive-equivalence instances. Reuse the proved sectionMonoidal_exists helper of FiniteComparisonPresentation, which assembles internal_section_tensor_comparison into CoreMonoidal using tensor naturality, associativity and the unit equations. The ringed cocontinuous restriction theorem applies to AsSmall.down and the coefficient isomorphism c, giving the remaining monoidal factor. Compose these structures for the actual functor discreteCoefficientModel. The scalar-restriction cancellation helper of ConstantScalarRestrictionTensor still proves its equivalence instance.

Since X is Noetherian it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so unfold internal constant-model constructibility as existence of a finite stratification with finite constant local models. On each stratum apply discrete_coefficient_local_models to its immersion and N. Convert finite-type constant local models to finitely presented ones by finiteLocalModels_iff_presentation. Apply proEtale_noetherian_global_constructibility in both directions, retaining the same stratification.

proof_origin.place: Integral-models proof (1)--(2): explicit normalized coefficient map, monoidal section and cocontinuous restriction, then finite local models on each stratum and the Noetherian global comparison. Q5 implements the first two parts and reduces only the local finite-model step.

lean.statement:
theorem discrete_coefficient_model (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (k : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing k] [IsNoetherianRing k]
    (e : ULift.{u + 1} A ≃+* k) :
    ∃ c : ConstantCompletion.constant (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} X) k ≅
        smallRing X (condensedRingObj (discreteObj A) X),
      DiscreteCoefficientNormalized X A k e c ∧
      Nonempty (discreteCoefficientModel X A k c).Monoidal ∧
      ∀ N, IsConstantModelConstructible (discreteObj A) X N ↔
        Scheme.IsCoefficientAffineLocallyConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf.{u, u} X k
          ((discreteCoefficientModel X A k c).obj N)
